field.label: Enable
field.help: Run the SurveillanceHound daemon at boot.

field.label: Listen interface
field.help: The NIC the surveillance traffic crosses. On OPNsense this is typically the camera VLAN or a SPAN/mirror port. Single interface only — use a BPF filter below to narrow within it.

field.label: BPF filter (optional)
field.help: Berkeley Packet Filter expression, e.g. "host 192.168.10.0/24".

field.label: Snaplen (bytes)
field.help: Bytes captured per packet for flow analysis. 96 covers all header layers; raise to 1500 if enabling snapshots.

field.label: Camera IPs
field.help: One IP per entry. Type a value and press enter to add it.

field.label: Camera subnets
field.help: One CIDR per entry. Anything in here is treated as a camera unless also listed as an NVR.

field.label: LAN subnets (optional)
field.help: Which prefixes count as "this network". Leave empty to treat RFC-1918 space as local. Add a tunnel or carrier-assigned range here if it looks public but is genuinely yours - otherwise traffic to it is scored as off-network telemetry, and a relay to a collector on it is refused.

field.label: Manufacturer allowlist (CIDRs)
field.help: One CIDR per entry: the vendor cloud your cameras legitimately talk to.

field.label: Silence threshold (seconds)
field.help: A camera with no observed packets for this long raises camera_offline. Detection is PASSIVE — Hound only watches traffic that crosses the listen interface, it never probes or pings the camera. A camera that is still powered and recording but no longer visible to this sensor (VLAN moved, mirror port reconfigured) looks exactly like one that is powered down. Default 600.

field.label: Track per-camera uptime
field.help: Record outage history and availability per camera, derived from observed traffic only (PASSIVE — no probing). Adds the camera_recovered, camera_never_seen and capture_stalled alert kinds. On by default.

field.label: Startup grace (seconds)
field.help: After the daemon starts, wait this long before alerting on a configured camera that has not been seen yet — otherwise every restart would fire camera_never_seen for cameras that are simply idle. 0 inherits the silence threshold above. Default 600.

field.label: Capture stall timeout (seconds)
field.help: Dead-man's switch: if ZERO packets at all are captured for this long, the sensor is blind, so one capture_stalled alert fires and per-camera offline alerts are suppressed until capture recovers. Without it a dead tcpdump looks identical to every camera failing at once. 0 disables. Default 120.

field.label: z threshold
field.help: Standard deviations from the bucket mean before an anomaly alert fires (default 4.0).

field.label: Min samples per bucket
field.help: Cold-start guard — no anomalies fire until each (camera, weekday, hour) bucket has this many observations.

field.label: Enable per-camera pcap snapshots on alert
Bind host
field.help: 127.0.0.1 keeps it loopback-only. Bind to a routable address only behind your own auth/proxy.

field.label: TLS cert (optional)
field.help: Absolute path to a PEM-encoded TLS certificate. Leave blank to inherit OPNsense's own UI scheme: HTTPS by default (a self-signed cert is auto-generated and stored under /var/lib/hound/), HTTP if OPNsense itself runs HTTP. The dashboard's scheme must match the firewall UI's or browsers block the embedded iframe as mixed content.

field.label: TLS private key (optional)
field.help: Absolute path to the matching PEM private key.

field.label: Relay role
field.help: Off is a single standalone sensor. Collector receives from agents elsewhere on your network - use this when cameras sit behind an NVR and their traffic never crosses the firewall, so this box cannot see them directly. Agent sends this box's own findings to another collector.

field.label: Listen address (collector)
field.help: The address agents connect to. Name a specific interface address; 0.0.0.0 is refused, because a relay listener should not be reachable from every interface by accident.

field.label: Listen port (collector)
field.help: Default 18443. Remember to add a firewall rule permitting your agents to reach it.

field.label: Ingest TLS cert (collector)
field.help: Absolute path to the PEM certificate the listener presents. Agents pin its fingerprint; run "hound relay" on this box to print the fingerprint to paste into each agent.

field.label: Ingest TLS key (collector)
field.help: Absolute path to the matching PEM private key.

field.label: Authorised sensors (collector)
field.help: One per line, as "id = shared-secret". Each agent signs every batch with its secret, and an id with no entry here is rejected. Give every agent its own id and its own secret.

field.label: Relayed history (days)
field.help: How long to keep relayed rows. 0 keeps them forever.

field.label: Row cap per sensor
field.help: Per table; the oldest rows are trimmed past this. An agent holding a valid key is still a host you do not control, so its data is bounded by count as well as by age. 0 disables.

field.label: Minimum free disk (MB)
field.help: Refuse relayed data below this much free space, so a remote sensor can never fill the disk local capture depends on. Agents spool and resend what is refused. 0 disables.

field.label: This sensor's id (agent)
field.help: Unique name for this box, as the collector will show it.

field.label: Collector URL (agent)
field.help: For example https://10.0.0.1:18443/ingest/v1 - https with an IP literal. A destination outside private space is refused unless it is covered by LAN subnets above.

field.label: Shared secret (agent)
field.help: Must match this sensor's entry in the collector's list.

field.label: Collector fingerprint (agent)
field.help: The collector's certificate is self-signed, so there is no CA to check it against and this pin is the trust decision. Run "hound relay" on the collector to print it. Verify it out of band the first time.
